items.title: Section: The Final Three Vows — Shared Path, Ceaseless Benefit, Swift Awakening — Closing All Ten Vows, With Their Alternate Names

items.zh: 為於一切在所生處，常不遠離諸佛菩薩，與諸菩薩常同一味意樂加行，是故引發第八大願。常為利益一切有情，曾不空過，是故引發第九大願。為證無上正等菩提，作諸佛事，是故引發第十大
items.en:
Eighth, for the sake of entering the same vehicle together. In order that, in every place of rebirth whatsoever, one never becomes far removed from the buddhas and bodhisattvas, always sharing with fellow bodhisattvas the very same single flavour of aspiration and application, this is why the eighth great vow is given rise to.
Ninth, for the sake of ceaselessly benefiting others. Constantly benefiting all sentient beings, never once spent in vain, this is why the ninth great vow is given rise to.
Tenth, for the sake of performing the buddhas' own undertakings. In order to realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening and perform every one of the buddhas' own undertakings, this is why the tenth great vow is given rise to.

items.title: Section: Vows Arising From a Vow — Endless as the Realm of Beings — Closing the Entire Third Aspect

items.zh: 願。作是願言：如有情界展轉相續，終無斷盡；亦如世道展轉相續，終無斷盡；我此大願生生相續，乃至究竟菩提邊際，常不遠離、常不忘失、常不乖離。如是自誓，心發正願。當知此中，前就所應願事起願，後即就願以起於願。如是菩薩十種大願以為上首，能生無數百千正願。如是菩薩，於當來世具諸大願，於現法中發大精進。
items.en:
Second, vows arising from a vow. One makes this vow: just as the realm of sentient beings continues on and on, never coming to an end; just as the way of the world continues on and on, never coming to an end; so too may this great vow of mine continue, life after life, all the way to the very boundary of ultimate awakening — never departed from, never forgotten, never contradicted. Taking this oath for oneself, one's mind gives rise to a correct vow.
Second, clarifying the brief meaning. One should understand that within this, the former vows arose from the specific matters one should vow about; the latter arose from the vow itself, giving rise to a further vow.
Commentary: Regarding "the former vows arose from the specific matters one should vow about" and the like — the ten great vows spoken of earlier are called vows arising from the specific matters one should vow about. The latter statement, that the vow never comes to an end, is called vows arising from the vow itself.
Third, the summary. These ten great vows of a bodhisattva, taken as the foremost concern, are able to give rise to countless hundreds of thousands of correct vows. Such a bodhisattva is thus equipped with every great vow for the world to come, and in the present life arouses great diligence.

items.title: Section: The Fourth Aspect Opens — Ten Dharmas That Purify Utmost Joy, Beginning With Pure Faith, Great Compassion, Great Loving-Kindness, and Giving

items.zh: 復有十種淨修住法，由是能令極歡喜住速得清淨。一者、於諸佛法深生淨信。二者、觀諸有情緣起道理，證得唯有純大苦蘊，發起大悲。三者、觀見彼已，自誓願言：我當令彼諸有情類，解脫如是純大苦蘊，得第一樂，發起大慈。四者、為欲救拔一切憂苦，自無顧戀；無顧戀故，能捨內外一切身財，於諸有情而行惠施。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: dharmas purifying the abode; first, naming the ten dharmas. There are furthermore ten dharmas that purify the abode, by which the abode of utmost joy is able to swiftly attain purity.
Second, listing each mark individually; first, pure faith. First, deeply arousing pure faith in the buddha-dharmas.
Second, great compassion. Second, observing the principle of dependent origination governing sentient beings, realising that this is nothing but a pure mass of great suffering, one arouses great compassion.
Third, great loving-kindness. Third, having observed this, one vows for oneself: I shall cause these very kinds of sentient beings to be liberated from this pure mass of great suffering and attain the foremost happiness — thus arousing great loving-kindness.
Fourth, giving. Fourth, in order to rescue beings from every anxiety and suffering, one is oneself entirely without attachment; being without attachment, one is able to relinquish both inner body and outer wealth entirely, giving generously to sentient beings.

items.title: Section: Purifying Dharmas Five Through Eight — Tireless Seeking, Mastering Treatises, Understanding the World, Cultivating Conscientiousness

items.zh: 五者、為欲利益諸有情故，從他勤求世出世法，曾無厭倦。六者、無厭倦故，證得一切論智清淨，善知諸論。七者、善知論故，於劣中勝諸有情所，如應如宜而修正行，善解世間。八者、即於如是正加行中，依應時分量等正行，而修慚愧。
items.en:
Fifth, being free of weariness. Fifth, in order to benefit sentient beings, diligently seeking worldly and world-transcending dharmas from others, never once growing weary.
Sixth, mastering treatises. Sixth, because of freedom from weariness, attaining a pure wisdom of every treatise, mastering treatises.
Seventh, understanding the world. Seventh, because of skilfully knowing treatises, for sentient beings of inferior, middling, and superior capacity, cultivating the right practice fittingly and appropriately for each, well understanding the world.
Eighth, cultivating conscientiousness. Eighth, precisely within this correct applied effort, according to what is fitting in time and measure, cultivating shame and conscientiousness.
Commentary: Regarding "according to what is fitting in time and measure" — the chapter on the hearers' stage, on abiding with correct understanding, says: whatever is to be done regarding this matter, this place, this time, according to measure, according to principle, according to its kind, one does exactly this matter, this place, this time, according to measure, according to principle, according to its kind, with correct understanding. (Fascicle 24, page 2066 of the Nanjing edition.) This statement, "according to what is fitting in time and measure," includes the remaining aspects as well, which should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Firm Resolve and Offering to the Tathāgata — Closing All Ten Purifying Dharmas With Their Summary

items.zh: 九者、即於如是正加行中，得無退轉堅力持性。十者、以諸上妙利養恭敬及與正行，供養如來。是名十種淨修住法。由此能令極歡喜住速得清淨。所謂淨信、慈、悲、惠捨、無有厭倦、善知諸論、善解世間、修習慚愧、堅力持性、供養如來。
items.en:
Ninth, firm, sustained resolve. Ninth, precisely within this correct applied effort, attaining an irreversible, firm, sustaining nature.
Tenth, offering to the Tathāgata. Tenth, with every kind of excellent offering, with reverence, and through right conduct, making offerings to the Tathāgata.
Third, summarising the brief meaning. These are called the ten dharmas purifying the abode. By these, the abode of utmost joy is able to swiftly attain purity — namely, pure faith, compassion, loving-kindness, generous giving, freedom from weariness, mastering treatises, understanding the world, cultivating conscientiousness, firm resolve, and offering to the Tathāgata.

items.title: Section: The Fifth Aspect Opens and Closes — Learning the Remaining Nine Abodes' Own Conduct, Attainment, and Result, Becoming a Great Guide

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於此十法受學、隨轉、多修習已，復於餘九增上戒等諸菩薩住，從佛菩薩專精訪求一切種道功德、過失，及神通樂、無失壞道，善取其行、得、等流相，於一切住自然昇進，證大菩提。為大導師，率領一切有情商侶，超度生死曠野嶮道。當知此中，諸行能入，說名為行；若正入時，說名為得；入已果利成辦圓證，說名等流。
items.en:
Fifth aspect: being shown the way towards the remaining abodes; first, skilfully grasping their mark. Furthermore, bodhisattvas, having received, practised, and repeatedly cultivated these ten dharmas, go on, towards the remaining nine abodes from heightened discipline onward, to seek out from the buddhas and bodhisattvas, single-mindedly and respectfully, every kind of path-quality, path-fault, joy of spiritual power, and unbroken path, skilfully grasping their conduct, attainment, and outflowing-result mark. In every abode, one naturally advances, realises great awakening, and becomes a great guide, leading every caravan of sentient beings across the perilous wilderness road of birth-and-death.
Commentary: Regarding "every kind of path-quality, path-fault" and the like — the skilful means present in each ground is called every kind of path. Being able to remedy every obstruction is called quality. The very obstruction being remedied is called fault. Spiritual power and transformation, entirely at will, is called joy of spiritual power. Knowing truly what is the path and what is not the path, and so not falling into the perilous wilderness road of birth-and-death, is called the unbroken path.
Second, explaining the terms conduct and the rest. One should understand that within this, the applied effort by which one is able to enter is called conduct; the very moment of correctly entering is called attainment; the complete, realised fruit once one has entered is called outflowing result.

items.title: Section: The Sixth Aspect Opens — Cultivating Wholesome Roots, Beginning With Two Causes for Beholding the Buddhas in This Very Life

items.zh: 又諸菩薩住此住中，由二因緣現見諸佛。
items.en: Sixth aspect: cultivating and purifying wholesome roots; first, presenting pure conditions; first, clarifying every case; first, making offerings to the three jewels; first, towards the buddhas; first, the cause of beholding them now; first, naming them. Furthermore, bodhisattvas dwelling in this abode, by two causes, behold the buddhas in this very life.

items.title: Section: The Two Causes Explained — Rough Pure Faith, and the Power of a Correct Vow

items.zh: 或由聽聞菩薩藏說，或由內心發起勝解，信有十方種種異名諸世界中，種種異名諸佛如來，由麁淨信俱行之心，求欲現見。如是求已，如實稱遂。當知是名第一因緣。又心發起如是正願：隨於彼彼諸世界中，有佛出現，我當往生。如是願已，如實稱遂。當知是名第二因緣。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas dwelling in this abode, by two causes, behold the buddhas in this very life.
First, rough pure faith. Whether through hearing what is proclaimed in the bodhisattva canon, or through an excellent understanding arisen from within, believing that throughout the ten directions, in world-systems bearing every kind of different name, there dwell buddha-tathāgatas bearing every kind of different name, with a mind accompanied by rough pure faith, one seeks to behold them directly. Having sought in this way, this is genuinely fulfilled exactly as sought. One should understand this as the first cause.
Second, the power of a correct vow. Furthermore, arousing in the mind this correct vow: wherever, among these various world-systems, a buddha appears, I shall go and be born there. Having made this vow, this is genuinely fulfilled exactly as vowed. One should understand this as the second cause.

items.title: Section: Offerings According to Capacity, Closing Out Offerings to All Three Jewels

items.zh: 菩薩如是由麁淨信現見諸佛，由正願力現見諸佛；既得見已，隨力隨能興一切種恭敬供養，奉施種種上妙樂具。及於僧眾恭敬供養。於如來所聽聞正法，無倒受持，精進修行法隨法行。
items.en:
Second, offering according to capacity. Bodhisattvas, thus beholding the buddhas through rough pure faith and through the power of a correct vow, having beheld them, arouse every kind of reverent offering according to their own power and capacity, respectfully presenting every manner of excellent, joyful offering-substance.
Second, towards the sangha. And towards the sangha, offering with reverence.
Third, towards the true dharma. In the buddha's presence, hearing the true dharma, receiving and upholding it without distortion, diligently practising dharma in accordance with dharma.

items.title: Section: Maturing Sentient Beings and Dedicating All Merit — Closing All Three Pure Conditions

items.zh: 以四攝事成熟有情。一切善根悉皆迴向無上菩提。
items.en:
Second, maturing sentient beings. Using the four means of attraction, maturing sentient beings.
Third, dedicating towards awakening. Every wholesome root is entirely dedicated towards unsurpassed awakening.

items.title: Section: The Summary and the Simile — Ore Refined by Fire, Closing the Entire Sixth Aspect

items.zh: 由是三種清淨因緣，彼諸善根倍復明淨。謂於佛法僧供養攝受故，以四種攝事成熟有情故，以一切善根迴向菩提故。如是乃至無量俱胝那庾多百千大劫。譬如世間黠慧工匠，以鑛性金置於火中，如如燒鍊，如是如是轉得明淨。如是淨勝意樂菩薩所有善根，由是三種清淨因緣，轉復明淨，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Second, presenting the brief meaning. By these three pure conditions, one's own wholesome roots grow doubly bright and pure — namely, through offering to and being embraced by the buddha, sangha, and dharma; through maturing sentient beings with the four means of attraction; and through dedicating every wholesome root towards awakening. This continues on, even to immeasurable koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of great eons.
Second, illustrating with a simile. Just as, in the world, a clever, skilful craftsman places ore containing gold into a fire, and the more it is smelted again and again, the more bright and pure it becomes — so too, a bodhisattva of pure, excellent aspiration, whatever wholesome roots are possessed, by these three pure conditions, grow ever more bright and pure in just this way. One should understand it is just so.

blocks.text: The great vows end with a famous line: they will last as long as the realm of beings. Then ten qualities that purify the first ground, and the simile of gold refined by a skilled craftsman.
Master Cháng Bǎi: buddhas are instructing friends, fellow bodhisattvas companion friends; "single flavour" is the Mahāyāna, everyone training in the same direction.

"As the realm of beings and the way of the world never end, may my great vow continue life after life to the boundary of awakening." Venerable Miào Jìng: a bodhisattva with acceptance of non-arising will not forget the vow in the next life.

Master Cháng Bǎi: pure faith contemplates ultimate truth, great compassion contemplates dependent origination. "I shall free those beings from this pure mass of great suffering and bring them the highest happiness."
Venerable Miào Jìng reads 解 as "relieving" beings' suffering; Master Cháng Bǎi reads it as "understanding": beings have many forms, and the bodhisattva has matching skill.
"Tenth, offering to the Tathāgata with every excellent offering, reverence, and right conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: the offering of Dharma is the true offering, foremost of all.
Venerable Miào Jìng: "arriving somewhere safe and prospering" is a metaphor; "seeking" means visiting teachers, bowing, learning, asking for instruction.
Venerable Miào Jìng: "rough" means shallow; seeing ultimate truth one sees the dharma-body buddha, not yet the emanation buddha. Master Cháng Bǎi: in absorption the buddhas truly appear.
Both lecturers: the first "dharma" is nirvāṇa; "according dharma" is the eightfold path.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the skilled craftsman is the bodhisattva who has aroused bodhicitta; the gold ore is their mind of false discrimination. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ore stands for wholesome roots such as faith, refined in fire.

The two teachers read the gold differently: as the mind being purified, or as wholesome roots being refined. Both readings work, and together they say the same thing: practice does not add something new; it removes what is mixed in.

quiz.q: The eighth vow — "always sharing a single flavour of aspiration and effort with bodhisattvas." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "single flavour"?
options: "single flavour" is the Mahāyāna — all training in one direction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: buddhas are instructing friends, fellow bodhisattvas companion friends; "single flavour" is the Mahāyāna — everyone training in the same direction.

quiz.q: "First vows from matters, then vows from the vow." What is the latter vow?
options: as the realm of beings and the world never end, may my great vow continue life after life until final awakening
quiz.why: "As the realm of beings and the way of the world never end, may my great vow continue life after life to the boundary of awakening." Venerable Miào Jìng: a bodhisattva with acceptance of non-arising won't forget the vow in the next life.

quiz.q: The second purifying dharma — great compassion from seeing beings as a pure mass of suffering. How does Master Cháng Bǎi contrast the objects of faith and compassion?
options: faith contemplates ultimate truth, compassion dependent origination — affliction, karma, and result are all suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: pure faith contemplates ultimate truth, great compassion contemplates dependent origination; afflictions, deeds, and results are all suffering. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: The third — great loving-kindness. What does the bodhisattva vow?
options: to free beings from the mass of suffering and bring them the highest happiness
quiz.why: "Having seen this, one vows: I shall free those beings from this pure mass of great suffering and bring them the highest happiness." Master Cháng Bǎi: wishing beings to realise the ultimate happiness of nirvāṇa just as oneself.

quiz.q: The seventh purifying dharma — "understanding the world (善解世間)." How do the lectures read it?
options: they differ — Miào Jìng: skilfully relieving the world's suffering; Cháng Bǎi: beings vary, the bodhisattva has matching skill — understanding the world
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng reads 解 as "relieving" — skilfully relieving beings' suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi reads it as understanding: beings have many forms and the bodhisattva has matching skill. The English also drops the "middling" class.

quiz.q: What is the tenth purifying dharma?
options: offering to the Tathāgata with excellent gifts, reverence, and right conduct
quiz.why: "Tenth, offering to the Tathāgata with every excellent offering, reverence, and right conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: dharma-offering is true offering, foremost of all.

quiz.q: "As a great guide, leading the caravan of beings across saṃsāra's perilous wilderness." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this image means?
options: reaching safety and prospering — a metaphor
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: arriving somewhere safe and prospering — it's a metaphor; "seeking" means visiting teachers, bowing, learning, asking for instruction.

quiz.q: The first cause of seeing buddhas — "rough pure faith." How do the lectures explain "rough"?
options: Miào Jìng: "rough" means shallow — seeing ultimate truth one sees the dharma-body, not yet the emanation body; Cháng Bǎi: still coarse compared with higher grounds; in absorption the buddhas appear
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "rough" means shallow; seeing ultimate truth one sees the dharma-body buddha, not yet the emanation buddha. Master Cháng Bǎi: compared with higher bodhisattvas the faith is coarser; in absorption the buddhas truly appear.

quiz.q: "Practising dharma in accordance with dharma (法隨法行)." How do the lectures explain "dharma" and "according dharma"?
options: both: "dharma" is nirvāṇa, "according dharma" the eightfold path
quiz.why: Both lecturers: the first "dharma" is nirvāṇa; "according dharma" is the eightfold path.

quiz.q: In the smelting simile, what does "ore containing gold" stand for? Do the lectures agree?
options: they differ — Miào Jìng: the craftsman is the bodhisattva, the ore their mind of false discrimination; Cháng Bǎi: the ore is wholesome roots such as faith
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the skilful craftsman is the bodhisattva who has aroused bodhicitta; the gold ore is their mind of false discrimination. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ore stands for wholesome roots such as faith, refined in fire.
